court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Family Court, Karur (H.M.O.P.No.11 of 2021 and H.M.O.P.No.100 of 2020)
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: V.Subramaniyan got married to P.Murugeshwari @ Muthamizhselvi on 06.02.2011. A male child Vaitheeswaran was born through the wedlock on 08.11.2011. The respondent / wife filed H.M.O.P.No.100 of 2020 for restitution of conjugal rights, while the appellant filed H.M.O.P.No.11 of 2021 for dissolving the marriage.

legal_principles.principle: The essence of desertion is forsaking and abandonment of one spouse by the other without reasonable cause and without consent or against the wish of the other.
legal_principles.held: To prove this ground, one must establish that there was not only a factum of separation but also the intention to bring cohabitation permanently to an end.

legal_principles.principle: A person who wants re-union cannot be said to be guilty of desertion.
legal_principles.held: The act of filing a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act itself falsifies the allegations made by the appellant.

legal_principles.principle: The burden is on the appellant to prove that he had made out a case for dissolving the marriage.
legal_principles.held: To do so, the appellant must show that his wife had committed one of the acts of misconduct set out in Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

outcome.final_order: The trial Court's judgment and decree dated 21.02.2022 in H.M.O.P.No.100 of 2020 and H.M.O.P.No.11 of 2021 were set aside, and the appeals were allowed.
